title: Joint measurability of coplanar POVMs
authors: Taro Yoshino, Koichi Tojo, Kei Hagihara, Akinori Tanaka, Takuki Tomita
abstract: An unbiased qubit positive operator-valued measure (POVM) can be uniquely expressed in terms of the Bloch vector. We prove that for POVMs with coplanar Bloch vectors, they are jointly measurable if and only if the perimeter of the convex closure of Bloch vectors is less than or equal to 4. Moreover, as a corollary, we give an affirmative answer to the conjecture suggested by [Andrejic-Kunjwal 2020] on the existence of a joint device for POVMs whose Bloch vectors lie on the same circle.
summary: This paper establishes a precise geometric criterion for determining when multiple quantum measurements (POVMs) on a qubit can be performed simultaneously (jointly measured). It proves that for coplanar measurements, joint measurability is equivalent to the perimeter of the convex hull of the associated Bloch vectors being at most 4. The methodology combines quantum information theory with advanced convex optimization techniques.
main_problem: The paper determines the necessary and sufficient conditions for the joint measurability (compatibility) of multiple unbiased binary qubit Positive Operator-Valued Measures (POVMs).
main_result: For coplanar POVMs, joint measurability is equivalent to the perimeter of the convex closure of their Bloch vectors being less than or equal to 4.
method: The problem is reformulated as a convex optimization problem involving minimizing a norm subject to linear constraints derived from the POVM structure.
model_or_system: The system involves unbiased binary qubit POVMs, which are characterized by their corresponding Bloch vectors $\mathbf{a}_i \in \mathbb{R}^3$. The analysis focuses on the geometric arrangement of these vectors.
key_observables: The Bloch vectors $\mathbf{a}_i$, the perimeter of the convex hull $\text{conv}\{\pm \mathbf{a}_i\}$, and the function $L(\mathbf{a}_1, \dots, \mathbf{a}_n)$.
important_parameters: The dimension of the space (2D vs 3D) and the value of the perimeter relative to 4 (or $L_n \le 1$ in general).
main_assumptions: The analysis initially focuses on the case where the Bloch vectors are coplanar ($\mathbb{R}^2$), and later relies on general convex optimization theory.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem equivalence using minimization techniques, derives the condition for the coplanar case using geometric arguments involving the convex hull, and confirms the result by solving the underlying convex optimization problem.
why_interesting: This work provides fundamental geometric constraints on the compatibility of quantum measurements, which is crucial for designing quantum information protocols and understanding measurement limitations.
